pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How does reading widely help us learn better?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read a text for information and enjoyment
   In simple words: practise until you can read a text for information and enjoyment. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: read a text for information and enjoyment

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Extensive Reading important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a passage based on how to select a text,
2. Read independently and silently,
3. Interpret what they read in their own way,
4. Discuss the topics of the texts with peers, 1. How does reading widely help us learn better? 2. What should one consider when choosing a reading text? 80

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does reading widely help us learn better?
2. What should one consider when choosing a reading text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a text for information and enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
